page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Marginal note in the right margin beside the line "fextertiorum". Below the text, a section heading (level 2) with the numbered title, then the next paragraph. No left margin, no foot notes, no catchword.

main_text.p: quinque asses deterreant? & post, Lucius Neratius pro delectamento habebat, os hominis liberi manus suæ palma verberare. Eum seruus sequebatur crumenam assium plenam portans: & quemcunque depalmauerat, numerari statim, secundum xii. Tabul. 25. asses iubebat. Propterea Prætores hanc legem abolescere & relinqui censuerunt, iniuriisque æstimandis recuperatores se daturos,edixerunt: & post, non omnino omnes iniurias ære isto pau-co diluerunt, tametsi hæc ipsa paucitas as-sium,graue pondus æris fuit. Nam libra-riis assibus in ea tempestate populus usus est: sed iniurias atrociores ut de osse[?] fra-cto[?],non liberis modo, verum etiam seruis factas impensiore damno vindicaverunt. hæc Gellius 20.c.1.

Paulus libro singulari,& titulo de iniuriis apud Ruffinum Titul. 2. Collationis legum Mosaicarum. Iniuriarum, inquit, astio[?] aut legitima est aut honoraria. Legiti-ma ex lege xii. Tabularum, Qui iniuriam alteri facit quinque & viginti festertiorum poena subit. quæ lex generalis fuit libero trecen-tas: *seruos CL. poenam subito sextertiorum.{a}Locus corruptus.
main_text.head: 2. De membro aut osse[?] fracto & Talione.
main_text.p: Phavorinus,Nonnulla autem in istis legibus nec consistere quidem (sicut dixi) visa sunt, Velut illa lex Talionis, cuius verba (nisi memoria me fallit) hæc sunt, Si membrum rupit [Festus legit rapserit in vocem Talionis] [illegible, ~10 letters]

page.notes: Marginal note "a. Locus corruptus." transcribed at right, marked in text as {a}. Doubtful readings: "ofle" (read as osse, long s taken as s); "astio" (word unclear, possibly aestimatio); "fra-cto" (ligature ﬅ read as st); "*" before seruos is a printed mark of uncertain meaning. The last line at the foot is very faint and partly illegible. Dots and a bullet at the bottom right are stains, not text. The page number is printed as "141" followed by a colon-like mark, which is not transcribed.
